title: Punishing an opening mistake

D0.outcome: Explains that an opening mistake (a premature attack, a pawn grab, an early queen sortie) is punished only when a concrete refutation exists in the position.

D1.outcome: Told that the opponent's last move was a mistake, finds the punishing sequence.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled opening positions, finds the punishment when it exists and develops calmly when it does not.

D3.outcome: Predicts which one-feature change (the development level, an open file) turns the punishment into a blunder.

misconceptions: Every opponent's mistake can be punished at once.
Taking a pawn early is always wrong.
conditions: Development is unfinished on the punished side.
contrasts: The same wing pawn is safe to take because the pieces are developed.
A centre pawn that really should be taken.
A developing move elsewhere is the point.
